subject: Re: Kickoff: LocoProp training-efficiency evaluation — status
body:
Hi Ximena, Bruno,

Status:

- Reproduction landed May 7. Both the squared-loss variant and the layerwise Bregman-divergence variants behave as published: on the benchmark models LocoProp closes most of the gap to the second-order baseline at essentially first-order memory. The parallel per-layer local updates are the key win — we get several local iterations per batch without blowing up step time.
- Head-to-head: job 1 (the abuse-classifier retrain) is done — 22% wall-clock reduction vs our current second-order setup at equal final AUC, and peak memory down 41%, which lets the job fit on half the GPUs. Job 2 (the trust-ranker) starts next week after Emeka finishes integration.

Risk: job 2 uses non-standard activations, and choosing the matching transfer function for the Bregman divergence isn't obvious — wrong choice degrades convergence. I've got two candidates; may cost us a week of sweeps. Saoirse's rating UI enters pilot Friday with 4 raters.

Giannis
